correctness.rationale: The commutator is the standard alternating dot product and the independent central coordinates contribute exactly t^2. An independent count avoids splitting the ring or using a generating character. Set n=2h, regroup into a pairing of two n-tuples, and fix the first tuple. The image of the pairing is its generated ideal and each target in the image has t^n divided by the ideal size preimages. If the tuple has a unit, this contributes (t^n-v^n)t^{n-1}=A-B to every target. Otherwise the image is the residue-field span of its coordinates in the radical, since the radical squares to zero. For a uniform radical tuple regarded as a linear map F_q^n to the radical, E(q^{-rank})=q^{-n}(1+(q^n-1)/v), by counting vectors in the kernel (each nonzero vector is sent to zero with probability 1/v). The zero fiber then receives the additional t^n v^n E(q^{-rank})=qB+(t-q)C. All nonzero radical targets receive the same additional weight by the GL_d action on the radical tuples and targets; their additional total, together with that at zero, is t^n v^n, giving q(B-C) for each nonzero target. Thus the precise three stated levels hold also in mixed characteristic. The level gaps tC and q(B-C) are positive and the unit level is positive. Pairing with coordinate unit vectors identifies the center; it equals the image and hence the derived subgroup. Dividing the zero count by t^{4h} gives the displayed commuting probability, and (v/t)^{4h}=q^{-4h} of all pairs have both horizontal vectors in the radical and automatically commute. The limiting fraction is conditional, not a claim that ordinary commuting probability tends to one. The provided checker and recorded output were inspected, not executed. Independently `python /workspace/branches/audit_checks.py heisenberg` checked rank one and two over the eight-element split ring by product-distribution convolution and verified the four-level Z/8 determinant comparator by direct enumeration.

value.rationale: Prescribed commutators refine ordinary commuting probability and connect directly to a natural determinant-counting question for local rings outside the classical principal class. The theorem computes every fiber in the nonprincipal square-zero class rather than just detecting that all targets are reached, and identifies an entire conditional commuting concentration regime. The exact comparison with Z/8 illustrates that the shape of this invariant, not just a normalization, can change at fixed ring size.
